title: Vector bundles for the colimit along Frobenius form a stack in groupoids for the h topology
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a prime p and a scheme S in characteristic p, the proposition asserts that the category fibred in groupoids over (Sch/S)_h whose fibre category over U is the category of finite locally free colim_F O_U-modules is a stack in groupoids, and that for quasi-compact and quasi-separated U the fibre category is colim_F Vect(U) (statement lines 12439-12450). The proof disposes of the final assertion by Lemma labelled lemma-colim-F-Vect, then verifies conditions (1), (2) and (3) of Lemma labelled lemma-refine-check-h-stack (proof lines 12452-12458). Condition (1) is immediate because glueing for the Zariski topology holds by definition; condition (2) is reduced, for a surjective flat proper finite presentation f : X -> Y with Y affine, to the equivalence Vect(Y) -> Vect(X) x_{Vect(X x_Y X)} Vect(X) obtained from fppf descent of finite locally free modules by Descent, Proposition labelled descent-proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent and Lemma labelled descent-lemma-finite-locally-free-descends, since the four schemes involved are quasi-compact and quasi-separated so that the description of fibre categories applies (proof lines 12460-12476). Condition (3) is the content of Lemmas labelled lemma-vector-bundle-I and lemma-vector-bundle-II (proof lines 12478-12483). Recognising that colimits of vector bundles are computed after fppf descent and that the remaining conditions are exactly the two almost blowup computations is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
